$comment: The threat register (SEC-001): every threat of 10 §3 tied to its control, the epic/story that builds it, and the SEC story whose tests prove it. A threat with no proving tests yet is marked "control-not-built" with the phase it is due. register.test.ts checks this file on every build (10 §2, §3, §5). Trust boundaries and actors follow 10 §2. specRows quotes the wording of 10 §3 that a row covers (a table row's threat, or a phrase of the prose in §3.4, §3.7 and §3.8); register.test.ts reads docs/spec/10-security.md and fails when a table row, a §3.7 item or a §3.8 sentence has no register row.

review.note: The end-of-phase review and the second-maintainer sign-off are SEC-003; this register and the SEC suite are its inputs. The sign-off is a human step and is not asserted here.

actors.trustedFor: identity, document-level role, group membership, how a participant was authenticated; holds a service credential
actors.hostile: no, but attribution is only as strong as the host's authentication

actors.trustedFor: holding the user's token; can do whatever that user can

actors.hostile: assume a user will send hand-crafted protocol messages

actors.trustedFor: nothing; also untrusted as input to an assistant model

actors.hostile: assume a worker can be fully compromised by the input it processes, and treat its outputs as hostile
tamper evidence that must hold against the operator needs chain heads anchored outside (08 §12)

threats.threat: Script injection through document content
threats.control: No raw HTML in the CDM; every attribute has a grammar (I11); DOM built with DOM APIs

threats.threat: Script injection through paste
threats.control: Pasted HTML sanitised then parsed through the schema

threats.threat: Dangerous links
threats.control: link.href allow-list (I9); noopener, noreferrer

threats.threat: Hostile images
threats.control: Never embedded as data; uploaded, validated and re-encoded; SVG never rendered live

threats.threat: A hostile PDF from a compromised worker
threats.control: Sandboxed cross-origin viewer with script off
specRows: A hostile PDF from a compromised worker

threats.threat: Token theft
threats.control: Tokens in memory only, never in URLs, short-lived, scoped to documents

threats.threat: Strict host policies
threats.control: CSP and Trusted Types requirements per feature; no HTML-string templates
threats.provenByNote: SEC-008 (Prove the component works under strict host policies) was merged into FE-125 in the cross-check of 2026-11-06, so FE-125 both builds and proves this row. Proposed reading, not an owner decision: docs/adr/0360-w3-SEC-001-register-proving-story.md.

threats.threat: Global side effects on the host page
threats.control: Hash-derived font aliases; shortcuts fire only inside the editor; duplicate element detected
specRows: Global side effects on the host page

threats.threat: Leaking content to the host page by accident
threats.control: Events carry identifiers and counts, not content
specRows: Leaking content to the host page by accident

threats.threat: Prompt injection through document text
threats.control: Untrusted text marked as data; side effects need approval; output only as escaped suggestions

threats.threat: Cross-site WebSocket use and cross-site request forgery
threats.control: Origin allow-list at hello; bearer tokens only, no cookies; CORS limited to tenant origins

threats.threat: Cross-tenant token confusion; a token that covers many documents
threats.control: Keys selected by tenant registration; asymmetric allow-list; exact audience; per-document roles
specRows: A token that covers many documents with one role

threats.threat: Reconnecting after revocation
threats.control: A revocation watermark refuses older tokens on both planes

threats.threat: Replay and resubmission; reused idempotency key
threats.control: Commit ids unique per document and bound to the user; idempotency keys scoped to tenant, caller, route, body
specRows: Taking over another caller's job through a reused idempotency key

threats.threat: Reaching someone else's thread, export or asset by its bare identifier
threats.control: Every resource resolved to its document and checked against the token
specRows: Reaching someone else's thread, export or asset by its bare identifier

threats.threat: Oversized or malformed messages
threats.control: Size limits, strict envelope parsing, close codes; the envelope parser is fuzzed

threats.threat: Resource exhaustion
threats.control: Limits per address, connection, user and tenant; bounded queues; admission control

threats.threat: Identity spoofing
threats.control: The server stamps user and session; client-supplied identity is checked or ignored

threats.threat: Forged webhooks and server-side request forgery
threats.control: Standard Webhooks signatures; an egress proxy refuses private addresses
specRows: Server-side request forgery through webhook targets

threats.threat: Changing a part of a document without permission
threats.control: The outcome check (07 §5.1), independent of step shape
specRows: Changing a part of a document without permission

threats.threat: Defacing protected text through shared styles
threats.control: A definition change needs edit or manage in every region that uses it (07 §5.3)
specRows: Defacing protected text through shared styles

threats.threat: Bypassing validation through rebase tricks
threats.control: Only mapped steps are applied, and they pass every check

threats.threat: Editing under permissions that were just revoked
threats.control: The log write is conditional on the grants revision (04 G7)
specRows: Editing under permissions that were just revoked

threats.threat: Corrupting the document
threats.control: Schema, invariant and attribute-grammar checks on every commit; step types on an allow-list

threats.threat: Stalling or crashing a process that hosts many rooms
threats.control: Admission control; CPU budgets; heavy work in worker threads; structural limits; fuzzing
specRows: Stalling or crashing a process that hosts many rooms

threats.threat: Forging history
threats.control: Server-side attribution; a hash chain over permission and workflow changes; anchored chain heads

threats.threat: Changing an approved region
threats.control: Approvals bound to a seq and a content hash; no commit of any origin may change an approved region

threats.threat: Two writers
threats.control: Epoch-checked writes and the log's primary key; self-fencing on the node lease

threats.threat: Reading deleted text through old versions
threats.control: One visibility gate on every sequence number a caller can supply (07 §8)
specRows: Reading deleted text through old versions

threats.threat: LaTeX injection
threats.control: Typed emitters for every context; escaping tested adversarially
specRows: typed emitters for every context in which a user's string can reach TeX

threats.threat: Equations that run code or paint over other text
threats.control: A strict math gate (I8) that bounds dimensions and removes overlap commands
specRows: a strict gate on math that also stops content painted outside its box

threats.threat: A compromised compile escaping the sandbox
threats.control: No shell escape, paranoid file access, no network, single-use sandbox, hard limits, no credentials

threats.threat: Worker outputs treated as trusted
threats.control: Outputs treated as hostile; layout schema-checked; logs bounded; results served nosniff

threats.threat: One compromised compile deciding what is sealed
threats.control: Two independent compiles are compared before sealing

threats.threat: Overwriting or claiming an asset; referencing one never uploaded
threats.control: Quarantine; the worker computes the hash and alone writes the final object; I4
specRows: Overwriting or claiming an asset by declaring its hash
Referencing an asset one never uploaded to gain read access to it

threats.threat: Decompression and pixel bombs
threats.control: Limits on entries, sizes and ratios; pixel limits; time and memory limits

threats.threat: XML external entities, remote content and macros in DOCX
threats.control: Reject DTDs and entities; never follow external relationships; refuse macros

threats.threat: Decoder exploits and content-type confusion
threats.control: Sandboxed worker without network or credentials; re-encode; detected type must match

threats.threat: Impersonation through imported tracked changes
threats.control: Imported authors become labels, never user identities

threats.threat: Stolen signing key
threats.control: Keys in an HSM or key service; signing service separate from every content worker

threats.threat: A tampered PDF being sealed
threats.control: Two independent compiles compared; the bundle pinned to a seq and chain head

threats.threat: Claims about signer identity the platform cannot support
threats.control: Records the host's authentication claims as given; product language follows 12 §8.3
specRows: Claims about signer identity the platform cannot support

threats.threat: Evidence leaking or outliving its purpose
threats.control: Evidence kept outside the log with its own retention; only salted hashes enter the chain
specRows: Evidence leaking or outliving its purpose

threats.threat: A filler changing more than their fields
threats.control: Rules P7 to P9, checked by the same outcome check
specRows: A filler changing more than their fields

threats.threat: One tenant reaching another's data
threats.control: Row-level security and a tenant id on every table, object path and cache key; per-tenant keys
specRows: Row-level security and a tenant identifier on every table

threats.threat: A leaked signed URL opening the whole store
threats.control: Short-lived, single-object signed URLs issued only after a permission check

threats.threat: Logs and metrics containing content or tokens
threats.control: Structured logs of known fields only; URLs redacted; errors by name
specRows: Logs and metrics never contain document content or tokens

threats.threat: Leaked secrets that cannot be rotated
threats.control: Secrets in a manager; webhook secrets and service credentials have rotation overlap
specRows: Secrets are held in a secret manager and rotated

threats.threat: A stolen backup file
threats.control: Backups encrypted; access audited; backup keys differ from live keys

threats.threat: A compromised or incompatible package entering the build
threats.control: Lock files, dependency review, install scripts off, licence policy

threats.threat: Not knowing what is inside a release
threats.control: A software bill of materials per release artefact
specRows: a software bill of materials per release

threats.threat: A swapped container image
threats.control: Signed images; base images pinned by digest
specRows: signed container images, pinned base images

threats.threat: A TeX Live update changing output or security
threats.control: A curated TeX Live pinned by digest with a licence manifest
specRows: a pinned TeX Live with a licence manifest

threats.threat: A third party changing what runs in the page
threats.control: The editor bundle loads scripts, styles, fonts and code only from configured origins
specRows: The editor bundle loads no code at run time from third-party origins

threats.threat: A sandboxed third-party extension reaching past its boundary
threats.control: Sandboxed third-party extensions are an explicit exception with their own review (13 §7.2; owner decision 120): a sandboxed frame with the one token allow-scripts, one private message channel, declared read and write levels checked by the host, writes through the guards of typing. The review record is docs/review/2026-11-18-ux-060-sandbox-review.md; its sign-off by a named person is open
specRows: The terms of the exception, and the first review of the sandbox

threats.threat: Parsers and emitters attacked continuously
threats.control: Fuzz targets registered, run on every change and kept as regression cases
